Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, today's conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions regarding muting lines and submitting questions via chat.]

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; and Casey Morgan, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of ShopNova.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust improvements in customer order frequency and accelerating adoption of our seller services, alongside efficient customer acquisition dynamics. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV up 20% year-over-year to $3.5 billion and active customers expanding by 15% to 16 million.

Our focus remains on enhancing mobile app engagement and preparing aggressively for the holiday season. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our expanded value-added services for sellers, which we believe will significantly boost our high-margin revenue streams.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience to counter logistics disruptions.

We are focused on improving order frequency through personalized recommendations and loyalty programs.

Finally, we are committed to driving seller services adoption to strengthen our marketplace ecosystem.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q2 revenue was $1.25 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, driven by a favorable mix shift toward higher-margin seller services and private-label products, partially offset by inbound freight pressures. Operating expenses were $465 million, representing 37.2% of revenue, reflecting disciplined growth investments. Our marketing spend held steady at 22% of revenue, delivering outsized returns as we'll detail shortly.

Our net income for the quarter was $135 million, or $0.92 per share. We ended the quarter with $850 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue between $5.1 billion and $5.3 billion, with adjusted EBITDA margins of 14-16%.

Let me dive deeper into some key drivers starting with customer acquisition cost dynamics and the efficiency of our marketing spend, which remain core to our profitability flywheel here at ShopNova. As a leading multi-category e-commerce platform—spanning home goods, apparel, and consumer electronics with over 15 million active customers—we've optimized our $450 million annual marketing budget to deliver industry-leading returns amid a challenging macro environment marked by rising ad platform costs and privacy headwinds.

For Q2 2024, our blended CAC came in at $42.30, a 12% improvement quarter-over-quarter from $48.10 in Q1 and a robust 18% decline year-over-year from $51.60 in Q2 2023. This efficiency stems from a 15% YoY increase in new customer adds—1.2 million in the quarter—while holding marketing expenses flat at 22% of revenue, down from 25% last year. Our Return on Ad Spend averaged 4.8x across channels, surpassing our internal target of 4.2x and up from 4.1x in Q1. This translates to a Lifetime Value to CAC ratio of 3.9x, well above the e-commerce benchmark of 3x, with a median customer payback period of just 7.2 months—compared to 9 months industry-wide per recent McKinsey data.

Breaking it down, our marketing mix has shifted toward high-ROI performance channels. Paid search, 35% of spend at $47 million in Q2, delivered 6.2x ROAS, fueled by Google Ads and Bing Shopping optimizations around high-intent queries like "sustainable kitchenware" and "wireless earbuds under $50." We're capturing 28% share of voice in these categories per SEMrush analytics, despite CPMs rising 8% YoY to $2.45 due to auction dynamics. Social media—primarily Meta and TikTok at 28% of budget or $38 million—clocked 4.5x ROAS, with TikTok's shoppable videos driving 22% of social-acquired orders, a 40% YoY uplift. Affiliates and influencers, 15% of spend, hit 5.1x ROAS via partnerships with creators in niches like #HomeRefresh.

Organic channels now comprise 42% of traffic, delivering near-zero marginal CAC. SEO investments in long-tail content like "best ergonomic office chairs for remote work" boosted organic new customer acquisition by 25% YoY per Google Analytics. Email and SMS retargeting via Klaviyo contributed 10% of traffic at under $5 CAC, with 32% open rates and 18% conversion lifts from dynamic recommendations.

Post-iOS 14.5 and Android Privacy Sandbox, we've reduced third-party cookie reliance from 65% to 38%, bucking industry CAC spikes of 20-30%. Our revenue per marketing dollar improved to $4.62 from $4.12 YoY. Our Customer Data Platform on Snowflake and Segment captures 85% signal accuracy via server-side tagging, up from 62%. AWS SageMaker models dynamically allocate budgets; our Predictive ROAS Optimizer shifted 12% of Meta spend to video ads, boosting incremental ROAS by 22%. We're piloting Google's Performance Max at 5.3x ROAS and investing $10 million in contextual targeting via The Trade Desk, while AI tools like Pencil cut ad production costs 35% and lifted CVR 14%.

Regionally, North America (78% of revenue) holds CAC at $38.50 with 5.1x ROAS, bolstered by Prime Day events driving 30% of volume. Europe (12%) dipped to €39 equivalent with 4.6x ROAS via localized Snapchat and SEO. APAC (8%) fell 25% to A$58 equivalent with 4.2x ROAS through Shopee and TikTok Shop in Indonesia, adding 250k customers despite India challenges mitigated by ONDC.

We're pursuing a retention-first flywheel, reallocating 18% of budget to bottom-funnel tactics for LTV >$350 customers. 2024 Q1 cohorts show 22% higher 12-month LTV with 48% Day 1 retention. Q3 CAC should trend to $40 with 5.0x ROAS, supported by holiday tests proving 65% Meta spend incrementality. This efficiency positions us for 25%+ adjusted EBITDA margins in FY24.

Shifting to order frequency, a key driver of top-line growth: trailing 12-month orders per active customer, or OPAC, rose 14% YoY from 4.2 to 4.8, our strongest acceleration since Q4 2021, outpacing peers like Chewy and Wayfair at 7-9%. Repeat revenue now accounts for 68% of GMV. Core categories like home essentials and beauty gained 16%, DTC private-label groceries 22%, reflecting snackable shopping with $25-50 micro-orders versus legacy bulk hauls.

Post-COVID, essentials cadence rose 28% for weekly consumables, mirroring Amazon Subscribe & Save at 40% Prime penetration. Inflation trimmed AOV 8% YoY to $62, but monthly orders hit 1.7 from 1.4. Gen Z (32% new adds) shows 5.6 OPAC via TikTok Shop.

North America (55% GMV) hit 4.5 OPAC with Walmart+ partnerships. Europe at 4.2 grew 12% via localized assortments. APAC starred at 5.5 with Shopee and India UPI. Our FastRecs 2.0 AI engine on transformer models lifted add-to-cart 17% and cross-sell 12%. ShopNova Prime at 45% penetration converts 23% one-timers to monthlies; OMS upgrades enable same-day in 72% urban areas, bumping frequency 31%.

We're scaling ARPU with CAC at $28, 15% below peers. Q3 OPAC at 12-13% YoY, full-year 4.9-5.0 with health subscriptions targeting 20% GMV by FY25. Tariff risks mitigated by 65% North American private labels.

Next, seller services and value-added services revenue totaled $285 million, up 28% YoY and 21% of total revenue. This outpaced 20% GMV growth to $3.5 billion, with 52% EBITDA margins above our 12% take rate.

Over 2.8 million active sellers, up 22% YoY, with 68% adopting at least one service—85% among top 20% by GMV. Advertising at $120 million (42%, +35% YoY) saw RPMs to $4.25 via AI ads; sponsored products 32% of search. Fulfillment at $88 million (+25%) hit 71% Prime adoption, $95 billion GFN GMV. Payments at $49 million (+32%) via ShopNova Pay at 2.8% of $120 billion GPV. Other services like analytics at $28 million (+22%) reduced stockouts 28%.

North America (55%) at 72% adoption; EMEA +34% to $60 million; APAC +42% to $71 million via WeChat; LatAm +18%. Flywheel: 2.7x GMV growth for users. Targeting 75% adoption by year-end with Pro tiers.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on logistics resilience amid supply chain disruptions and holiday inventory positioning. Total logistics expenses rose 28% YoY to $512 million or 12.2% of revenue, with cost per unit at $4.76, up 22% from parcel surcharges and ocean freight at $3,800/FEU due to Red Sea reroutings adding 10-14 days. U.S. port dwell at 7.2 days; North America last-mile up 32% to $2.18/package; Europe inbound +40%; APAC monsoon delays.

We've optimized with AI TMS reducing dwell 22%, drone pilots, and micro-fulfillment—12 sites now. Nearshoring 25% electronics to Mexico saves 35%; 70% H2 hedged 15% below spot. Q3 flat sequentially, full-year 11.5-12% of revenue.

For holidays, inventory at $2.1 billion or 125% last year's peak, 2.1x sales ratio. Electronics $735 million (35%), apparel $525 million (25%), home $420 million (20%). U.S. 55%, Europe 25% localized, APAC 15% for Singles' Day. NovaForecast AI at 96% accuracy projects $4.8 billion Q4 GMV (+22%), BFCM $1.68 billion. RFID cuts shrinkage to 0.8%; 45% eco-certified.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from performance search and TikTok shoppable videos, tying into our CAC efficiency. Customer acquisition costs were $42.30 with 4.8x ROAS. Our brand awareness increased by 25% per surveys. We are focusing on retention-first tactics targeting high-LTV segments.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey.

Casey Morgan:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on mobile app enhancements and AI supply chain tools. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 32% YoY. We're investing in edge computing for personalization and Web3 loyalty.

Specifically on mobile app engagement: 4.2 million downloads (+28% YoY), DAU 1.8 million (+32%), MAU 14.5 million (+25%), DAU/MAU 12.4%. Conversions at 7.9% vs. web 4.2%, driving 68% GMV. Day 1 retention 48%. North America 8.4% conversions; APAC 7.1%. Firebase pushes at 41% opens; app v8.0 upcoming.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions for Q&A]. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, can you expand on the CAC improvements and how sustainable they are heading into holidays with ad costs rising?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Absolutely, our $42.30 CAC reflects strategic shifts to high-ROI channels like paid search at 6.2x and organic at zero marginal cost. With privacy changes, our first-party data CDP at 85% accuracy and SageMaker optimizers ensure sustainability. Holidays will see Q3 at $40 with 5.0x ROAS via incrementality tests—very sustainable.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Patel:
Great, thanks. Alex or Jordan, on order frequency—4.8 OPAC is impressive. What habit changes are driving this, and any regional differences?

Alex Rivera:
Lisa, thanks. The shift to snackable $25-50 orders from bulk, plus 28% essentials cadence rise, drives it. Gen Z at 5.6 OPAC via social. North America 4.5 with partnerships, APAC 5.5 strongest. FastRecs AI and Prime nudges sustain this.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with JPMorgan.

David Ruiz:
Thanks. Taylor, logistics costs up to 12.2%—how are disruptions impacting, and mitigation timeline?

Taylor Kim:
David, Red Sea and ports drove $3,800/FEU and 7.2-day dwells. Nearshoring to Mexico saves 35%, hedges lock 70% volume. Q3 flatlines, H2 savings $50 million push us under 12% full-year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Wong with Barclays.

Emma Wong:
Hi, team. Riley, seller services at 21% of revenue—adoption details and impact?

Riley Patel:
Emma, 68% seller adoption, 85% top tier. Ads $120 million at $4.25 RPM, fulfillment 71% Prime. Drives 2.7x GMV uplift for users, 45% of revenue growth—key moat.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Singh with Citi.

Raj Singh:
Thanks. Casey, mobile app metrics look strong—downloads, DAU, conversions—and tech roadmap?

Casey Morgan:
Raj, 4.2 million downloads, 1.8 million DAU, 7.9% conversions driving 68% GMV. App v7.2 Smart Feed boosts retention to 48% D1. Q3 v8.0 adds Web3 and edge AI for iOS 18.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders—leveraging CAC efficiency, frequency gains, seller services growth, resilient logistics, app engagement, and holiday readiness. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
